english.title: Permit premises to be open in contravention of a police closure order - Licensing
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) without reasonable excuse permitted relevant premises, namely **(..SPECIFY THE PREMISES..), to be open in contravention of

(A)_[a closure order]_
(B)_[an extension to a closure order]_

made under section 161 of the Licensing Act 2003
english.legislation: Contrary to section 161(6) and (7) of the Licensing Act 2003.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: From 20th October 2014, the power to make an order under section 165 of the Licensing Act 2003 is no longer in force. The repeal does not, however, apply in relation to an order made before that date or anything done in connection with such an order. As such, this offence can still be committed in relation to premises subject to an order made before 20th October 2014.

other.penalty:
Three months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding twenty thousand pounds

Time limit for prosecutions:
12 months
